cards.title: Introduction to Spring Boot Testing
cards.content:
Spring Boot provides excellent support for automated testing across different layers of your application. It categorizes tests into two main types:

  • Unit Tests: Test individual components in isolation without loading the Spring ApplicationContext.
  • Integration Tests: Test components together, often starting a full or partial Spring ApplicationContext.

The spring-boot-starter-test dependency automatically imports JUnit 5, Mockito, AssertJ, and Spring Test modules.

cards.title: Unit Testing with JUnit 5 & Mockito
cards.content:
When unit testing service classes, isolate them using Mockito. Use @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) to enable Mockito annotations.

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class UserServiceTest {
    @Mock
    private UserRepository userRepository;

    @InjectMocks
    private UserService userService;
}

content.question: Which annotation is used in JUnit 5 to enable Mockito extensions?

cards.title: Mocking Spring Beans with @MockBean
cards.content: When testing within a Spring Context (e.g., Integration or Slice tests), standard @Mock isn't registered in the Spring Container. Use @MockBean to add a Mockito mock into the Spring ApplicationContext, replacing any existing bean of the same type.

content.sentence: To replace a bean with a Mockito mock inside the Spring ApplicationContext, use the annotation _____.

cards.title: Testing Web Layer with @WebMvcTest
cards.content:
@WebMvcTest is used for slice testing REST Controllers. It disables full autoconfiguration and loads only beans relevant to Web MVC (e.g., Controllers, ControllerAdvice, Filters).

@WebMvcTest(UserController.class)
class UserControllerTest {
    @Autowired
    private MockMvc mockMvc;

    @MockBean
    private UserService userService;
}

content.instructions: Order the steps to build and verify a MockMvc HTTP request test.

cards.title: Data JPA Testing with @DataJpaTest
cards.content:
@DataJpaTest focuses only on JPA components. It configures an in-memory database by default, scans for @Entity classes, and configures Spring Data JPA repositories.

By default, tests annotated with @DataJpaTest are transactional and roll back at the end of each test.

pairs.right: Loads complete ApplicationContext for integration tests
Focuses only on Spring MVC components (Controllers)
Focuses only on JPA repositories and entities with transactional rollback
